I am the second oldest of 5 siblings. We are 21 M 19F (me) 16F, 13M 9F. Every year since my youngest sister was born we have been doing funny photo shoots for my mom’s birthday. We put the photos into a giant card and all go out shopping for her birthday present. This has become a tradition that has gotten better and better over the years. My Mom always loves it and collects the cards. Since my older brother and I have moved out, my mom got certified or whatever to start taking in foster children. They have one (14 or 15ish? F) that’s been staying at the house for like four months. Here’s the dilemma: I don’t want her in the pictures. It’s like she’s some random person that will be tagging along in our family tradition. From the outside looking in am I (and my brother I guess) being an A-hole? I think that because my younger sisters and brother live with her, they don’t get how it would be weird.

So, is it right or wrong for the older siblings not to want the foster kid in the photo? Let's consider different perspectives. On one hand, the older siblings have a long-standing tradition that's very personal to them. They've been doing this since the youngest was born, and it's something they've all looked forward to and participated in. Including someone new, especially someone who might not be a permanent part of the family, could disrupt that tradition. They might feel that the foster kid isn't part of their close-knit group, and adding her could make the photos feel less personal or meaningful. On the other hand, the foster kid is living with them, and the younger siblings have formed a bond with her. They see her as part of their family, at least temporarily, and want her to be included in their activities. Excluding her could make her feel unwelcome or like an outsider, especially since she's been with them for several months. It might also make the younger siblings feel like their feelings and opinions don't matter, leading to tension within the family. Another angle to consider is the foster kid's feelings. It's important to think about how she might feel and whether her inclusion would make the family photo more inclusive and welcoming.
